title: Signature Layered-Defense Ledger
description: Signature edition: every obfuscation layer is recorded with its measured potency, resilience, and cost — the ledger justifies each layer with numbers. When a layer is defeated (deobfuscator published), the ledger flags it and the defense plan adapts. Obfuscation managed like a security control, not a hope. This is a Signature original method.
method: Log per-layer (potency, resilience, cost); monitor the deobfuscation literature; flag defeated layers; adapt the plan.
usage: Review the ledger when new deobfuscation techniques appear; rotate defeated layers out.

demo.code:
print('layer: VMProtect v3 (potency high, cost 12%)')
print('new paper deobfuscates VMProtect v3 -> FLAGGED, migration to v4 scheduled')

title: Signature Opaque predicates
description: Signature edition: Opaque predicates are branches whose outcome the obfuscator knows but analysis can't easily determine — 'if (x*x >= 0)' is always true for integers, but proving it takes work. Sprinkled through flattened code, they add fake paths that waste reversers' time on branches that never take.
method: Insert always-true/false predicates guarding junk code; base them on invariants hard to prove (number theory, aliasing).
usage: Vary predicate families (one family is learnable); don't let junk code affect semantics.

demo.code:
x = 7
print(f'opaque: if ({x}*{x} >= 0): real_path() else: junk_path()')
print('always true for ints; reverser must prove it')

title: Signature Mixed boolean-arithmetic (MBA) expressions
description: Signature edition: MBA replaces simple operations with convoluted equivalents: x + y becomes a mess of XORs, ANDs, and multiplications that's provably equal but painful to simplify. Reversers' deobfuscators choke on MBA; it's the arithmetic equivalent of control-flow flattening.
method: Rewrite arithmetic as MBA identities; verify equivalence; apply to license checks and crypto-adjacent code.
usage: Apply to critical computations; verify the MBA identity's correctness formally.

demo.code:
print('x + y  ->  (x ^ y) + 2*(x & y)  ->  MBA-expanded 14-term form')
print('provably equal; simplifiers struggle')

title: Signature Anti-debugging techniques
description: Signature edition: Obfuscated code fights back against debuggers: timing checks (rdtsc deltas reveal single-stepping), debugger-presence APIs (IsDebuggerPresent, ptrace), and exception-based control flow that breaks under debuggers. Each technique is bypassable, but layered they raise the cost of dynamic analysis.
method: Layer timing checks, presence detection, and anti-attach; respond by degrading (not crashing — crashes confirm the check worked).
usage: Layer several; respond subtly; assume each will be bypassed eventually.

demo.code:
import time
t0 = time.perf_counter()
# ... protected region ...
dt = time.perf_counter() - t0
print(f'region took {dt*1e6:.0f}us', '-> debugger suspected' if dt > 0.1 else '-> clean')

title: Signature Watermarking and fingerprinting
description: Signature edition: Obfuscation hides; watermarking traces: embed per-customer fingerprints in the binary (instruction choices, basic-block orderings) so leaked copies identify the leaker. The code runs identically for everyone but each build is uniquely traceable.
method: Vary codegen choices per customer (register allocation, block order); record the fingerprint; extract from suspect binaries.
usage: Fingerprint high-value distributions; keep the fingerprint database secure.

demo.code:
print('build for customer C7: block order [3,1,2], regalloc seed 77')
print('leaked binary analyzed -> fingerprint matches C7')

title: Signature Obfuscation measurement (potency/resilience)
description: Signature edition: Collberg's framework measures obfuscation: potency (how much harder to understand), resilience (how hard to deobfuscate automatically), cost (performance hit). Measuring turns obfuscation from vibes into engineering — you know what each layer buys and what it costs.
method: Measure before/after complexity metrics; test against deobfuscators; track the cost budget; drop layers that don't pay.
usage: Measure every layer; keep what pays; the cost budget is real.

demo.code:
print('flattening: potency +62%, resilience high, cost +8% -> KEEP')
print('MBA: potency +40%, cost +31% -> DROP (over budget)')

title: Signature Symbol stripping and renaming
description: Signature edition: The first obfuscation everyone applies: strip symbols, rename everything to meaningless identifiers. It doesn't stop a determined reverser, but it removes the free documentation — function names like 'verify_license' become 'a1b2c3', and the reverser starts blind.
method: Strip debug symbols; rename identifiers systematically; remove metadata; verify the build still links.
usage: Always strip release builds; renaming is table stakes, not protection.

demo.code:
print('before: verify_license(), check_expiry()')
print('after: a1(), b7() (stripped, renamed)')

title: Signature Virtualization obfuscation
description: Signature edition: The strongest practical layer: compile the sensitive function to bytecode for a custom random VM, and ship the VM interpreter. Reversers must first reverse-engineer the VM itself — its instruction set, handlers, and dispatch — before they can even see the protected logic. VMProtect and Themida work this way.
method: Define a custom ISA; translate the function to it; emit the interpreter + bytecode; virtualize the critical paths.
usage: Virtualize only the crown jewels (performance cost is high); randomize the VM per build.

demo.code:
print('function check_license() -> VM bytecode [0x3F, 0xA1, ...]')
print('reverser must first RE the custom VM (200 handlers) before seeing logic')

title: Signature String and constant encryption
description: Signature edition: Plaintext strings ('license expired', API keys, URLs) are reverser gold. Encrypting all constants — decrypted at runtime just before use, wiped after — removes the easy landmarks. The binary's strings section becomes noise.
method: Encrypt constants at build; emit decrypt-on-use stubs; wipe after use; rotate keys per build.
usage: Encrypt all sensitive constants; JIT-decrypt to minimize exposure window.

demo.code:
print('strings section: no "license", no URLs (all encrypted)')
print('runtime: decrypt -> use -> wipe (exposure: microseconds)')
